companies.bayNote: San Francisco Bay Area = the metros covering the nine Bay Area counties: San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont, San Jose-Sunnyvale-Santa Clara, Santa Rosa-Petaluma, Napa, Vallejo.

list.name: AT&T
list.notes: AT&T's US postings give one range and no zones. For its field and retail sales roles the range includes salary and commission. Its union job families (CWA, IBEW) are left out of pay search.
list.basis_quote: Individual starting salary within this range may depend on geography, experience, expertise, and education/training

list.name: Activision Blizzard
list.notes: Activision, Blizzard and King (part of Microsoft) post one range “across all U.S. locations” and no zones. Hourly roles are left out of the pay ranges here.
list.basis_quote: your specific range and offer will be based on several factors, including relevant experience, performance, and work location

list.name: Adobe
list.notes: Adobe's US postings give one US range and say it pays differently by “defined markets” it doesn't name. Most also add a range for the job's own state (California, New York, Washington, Illinois, Massachusetts or Colorado); those aren't shown here yet.
list.basis_quote: Pay within this range varies by work location

list.name: Affirm
list.notes: Affirm's postings give one base pay range for California, Washington, New York, New Jersey and Connecticut and another for all other US states. They don't call them zones; we use their wording as the names. Read on 83 of its current postings.
list.basis_quote: based on a variety of factors, including location

list.name: Airbnb
list.notes: Airbnb's US postings give one pay range and no zones. Its postings list training, skills, experience, business needs and market demands as what sets pay, not location.

list.name: Airtable
zones: SF Bay Area, Seattle, LA, New York
list.notes: Airtable's postings give two ranges and name the places for the higher one. We matched each to its metro.
list.basis_quote: For work locations in the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, Los Angeles, and New York

list.name: Amazon
list.notes: Amazon posts a range for each city a role is open in and publishes no zone list. We group its cities by metro: each place here lists the cities Amazon's current postings name in that metro, and a posting's range for each of those cities shows for it. Cities outside any metro and “Virtual Location” ranges are left out. AWS, Ring, Zappos and Audible hire through amazon.jobs.
list.basis_quote: Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location

list.name: American Express
list.notes: American Express's US postings give one expected salary range and no zones; in the postings we read, the same range showed in New York and Phoenix.
list.basis_quote: Ultimately, in determining your pay, we’ll consider your location, experience, and other job-related factors

list.name: Anthropic
list.notes: Anthropic's US postings give one annual range covering every office the role lists, and no zones. For sales roles the range is on-target earnings.

list.name: Apollo.io
list.notes: Apollo.io's postings give a Tier 1 range for San Francisco, New York City and Seattle and a Tier 2 range for all other US locations, the same in 19 of its 45 postings on 24 Nov. We match each city to its metro; Apollo.io names San Francisco, not the whole Bay Area, so San Jose and the rest of the Bay Area show Tier 2.

list.name: Apple
list.notes: Apple posts a range for each office a role is open in, and publishes no zone list. We group its offices by metro: each place here lists the offices Apple's current postings name in that metro. Offices in states without a pay-range law (Texas, among others) show no range. Postings that name only the “San Francisco Bay Area” are left out, since that spans two metros. Hourly ranges are left out.
list.basis_quote: your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location

list.name: Asana
list.notes: Long Island and Newark are inside the New York-Newark-Jersey City metro.
list.basis_quote: based on your specific home location

list.name: Atlassian
list.notes: Atlassian defines zones by county, and doesn't publish the county list. We count the Tri-State Area as the New York metro plus Bridgeport-Stamford, CT.
list.basis_quote: based on your specific home location / county

list.name: BILL
list.notes: BILL (Bill.com) lists three geographic zones in its job postings, the same in all 37 on 24 Nov. We match by metro: BILL's Zone 1 names Los Angeles County, so Orange County (in the Los Angeles metro) shows Zone 1 here, and "New York City" is matched as the New York metro. The rest of Texas isn't listed.
list.basis_quote: based on a variety of factors including candidate experience, expertise, and geographic location

list.name: Benchling
list.notes: Anywhere within 100 miles of a listed city takes that city's zone; we match by metro only, so check if you're near one. We put all of New York state outside the NYC metro in Zone 2, but Benchling says places within 100 miles of the city are Zone 1.
list.basis_quote: If your work location is within a 100 mile radius of a hiring location

list.name: Block
list.notes: Block lists cities, not metros; we matched each to its metro. Places about 50 miles outside a listed metro may be in a different zone. Scottsdale is in the Phoenix metro.
list.basis_quote: work locations that are approximately 50 miles outside of the metro area

list.name: CVS Health
list.notes: CVS Health's US postings give one typical range for the role's job grade and no zones. Most of its postings are store and pharmacy jobs paid hourly; pay search shows its office roles.
list.basis_quote: The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors

list.name: Calendly
list.notes: Calendly lists its tiers in job postings; we matched each city to its metro. Its postings also say it's registered as an employer in many, but not all, states.
list.basis_quote: the zip code of an employee's remote work location, or the onsite building location if hybrid

list.name: Calix
list.notes: Calix doesn't name its zones; the names here are its group headings. Raleigh-Durham covers the Raleigh-Cary and Durham-Chapel Hill metros.

list.name: CircleCI
list.notes: CircleCI's highest zone is called Metro Zone 3; its postings say the metro list may change periodically.

list.name: Cisco
zones: Non-Metro New York state & Washington state
list.notes: Cisco's postings list full salary ranges for these two areas, the same in all 199 US postings read on 25 Nov. Elsewhere they give a starting range for “U.S. and/or Canada locations”, which isn't a zone and isn't shown. For quota-based sales roles the ranges include base pay plus target incentive.
list.basis_quote: Individual pay is determined by the candidate's hiring location

list.name: Coca-Cola
list.notes: The Coca-Cola Company's US postings give one range for the United States and no zones.
list.basis_quote: Base pay offered may vary depending on geography, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience

list.name: Cohere
list.notes: Cohere lists two US pay tiers in its job postings, by state. A few postings add Washington DC to the higher tier.

list.name: Coursera
list.notes: Coursera lists its four US zones in its job postings.
list.basis_quote: zone-based pay aligned to your location

list.name: Databricks
list.notes: Databricks sets zones by state only, with no metro rules.

list.name: Deepgram
list.notes: Deepgram's postings give each level a range for SF, NYC and Seattle and one for everywhere else.

list.name: Disney
list.notes: The Walt Disney Company posts a range for each city a role is open in and publishes no zone list. We group its cities by metro: each place here lists the cities Disney's current postings name in that metro, and a posting's range for each of those cities shows for it. Left out: remote roles (one range that, Disney says, factors in geographic regions), ranges given for a whole state or for two cities at once, and cities outside any metro.
list.basis_quote: The base pay actually offered will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate’s geographic region

list.name: Dropbox
list.published: in job postings (this one updated Nov 2026)
list.notes: Dropbox lists its zones in each job posting. Anywhere within 100 miles of a listed metro takes that metro's zone, by your home zip code; we match by metro only, so check if you're within 100 miles of one. Its postings set the zone by the zip code of your remote work location.

list.name: Elastic
list.notes: Elastic says its higher range applies in select locations "including" these four, so other places may also qualify. Ask the recruiter.

list.name: Etsy
list.notes: Etsy lists its two zones in its job postings and doesn't define the metro edges. Its postings say base salary is set by your location.
list.basis_quote: Base salary is determined by your location

list.name: GitHub
list.notes: Every current GitHub US posting with a range (77 on 25 Nov) gives one range for the whole US and says location is one of the things that sets base pay. Where a place lands in the range isn't published; ask the recruiter.
list.basis_quote: An individual's base pay depends on various factors including geographical location

list.name: Google
list.notes: Google's US postings give one “US” range plus a bonus target, equity and benefits, and no zones; postings open in several states still show one range. YouTube and Google DeepMind hire through Google's site.

list.name: Humana
list.notes: Humana's US postings give one starting base range and no zones. Many are home health and clinical roles.
list.basis_quote: The pay range may be higher or lower based on geographic location

list.name: Included Health
list.notes: Included Health gives example cities for each zone ("e.g."), not a full list, so only those cities are matched here. Its Zone D is the highest-paid and Zone A the lowest. Its postings give one range across the zones, so there's no range per zone.
list.basis_quote: individual pay is determined by work location

list.name: Indeed
list.notes: Indeed has a Tier 4 with no US locations right now. Its regions (Northeast, Mountain and so on) are drawn on maps; we read the states off those maps.
list.basis_quote: confirm your applicable pay tier based on your work location

list.name: Instacart
list.notes: Instacart lists pay by state groups in its job postings without naming them; we number them from highest pay. Its postings say pay depends on your permanent work location.
list.basis_quote: dependent on their permanent work location

list.name: Intel
list.notes: Intel's US postings give one range “across all US locations” and no zones. Contract and student postings share one broad range.
list.basis_quote: Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors

list.name: Lambda
list.notes: Lambda's tiers are named for its offices, with remote US work as the third. We matched each office to its metro.

list.name: LaunchDarkly
list.notes: LaunchDarkly lists its zones in job postings and defines them by county, without a county list. It puts Santa Rosa in Zone 2 even though it's part of the Bay Area. Irvine is in the Los Angeles metro, and Monterey is in the Salinas metro.

list.name: Lockheed Martin
list.notes: Lockheed Martin's postings list four GeoZones, each with example metro areas (“such as … etc.”), not a full list. We map only the places it names, by metro: Sunnyvale and Palo Alto are the San Jose metro, Newark is in the New York metro, and King of Prussia and Moorestown are the Philadelphia metro. Camden, AR and Lufkin, TX (GeoZone 4) are in no metro. Most on-site postings give one range for their site with no GeoZone named; only the GeoZone ranges, from remote postings, are shown here.
list.basis_quote: Locations are assigned a Geo Zone based on the primary work location of the role

list.name: Marqeta
list.published: No date shown (updated annually, the page says)
list.notes: Marqeta's page lists regions by state and area with a tier for each. We match its areas to metros: the NY metro tri-state area as the New York metro plus Bridgeport-Stamford (Connecticut's part of the tri-state area); Seattle as the Seattle metro. Southern New Jersey, other Connecticut and the rest of Washington are National.
list.basis_quote: We calibrate pay to working location

list.name: Mercury
zones: NYC, LA, Seattle, SF Bay Area
list.notes: Mercury's postings give two ranges: one for the four named areas and one for everywhere else in the US.
list.basis_quote: US employees in New York City, Los Angeles, Seattle, or the San Francisco Bay Area

list.name: Meta
list.notes: Read by hand from a Software Engineer, Product posting (Sunnyvale and 7 other locations) on 26 Nov: one range for the United States of America and no zones. Meta's site doesn't allow automated reads, so there are no Meta ranges in pay search.
list.basis_quote: Individual compensation is determined by skills, qualifications, experience, and location

list.name: Microsoft
zones: SF Bay Area and NYC metro
list.notes: Microsoft's postings give a range across the US and a higher one for specific work locations in the San Francisco Bay Area and New York City metro, without naming which places count. We use the Bay Area metros and the New York metro.
list.basis_quote: will depend on what ultimately is determined to be the candidate's primary work location

list.name: Modern Health
list.notes: Modern Health lists all four zones in its job postings, covering every state.
list.basis_quote: individuals applying to work remotely from the following locations

list.name: Netflix
list.notes: Netflix's US postings give one range per role and no zones; pay is all salary (no bonus), and you choose the salary and stock mix. The location sentence is on remote and multi-city postings. “Overall market” ranges and hourly ranges are left out here.
list.basis_quote: This compensation range will vary based on location

list.name: Nvidia
list.notes: Nvidia's US postings give one range, or one per level (Level 4, Level 5), and no zones. Sales roles give cash compensation, 85% base and 15% variable.
list.basis_quote: Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors

list.name: Okta
list.notes: Okta's postings give two ranges and name the places for each, but don't call them zones.
list.basis_quote: for candidates located in the San Francisco Bay area

list.name: Omada Health
list.notes: Omada sets zones by state only, with no metro rules. Its postings say your zone is set by your location.
list.basis_quote: the range applicable to your zone (which is determined by your location)

list.name: OpenAI
list.notes: OpenAI's US postings mostly give one range for the role's office, usually San Francisco, and no zone list. Some remote postings add “Zone A” and “Zone B” ranges without saying which places those cover; those aren't shown here.
list.basis_quote: The base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience

list.name: Oracle
list.notes: Oracle's US postings give one US hiring range and no zones.
list.basis_quote: Oracle maintains broad salary ranges for its roles in order to account for variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions and locations

list.name: Plaid
list.notes: Plaid's full list is in one posting; other postings show only some zones and sometimes label them differently (one Raleigh posting says Zone 1). Confirm with the recruiter. We matched each city to its metro.

list.name: Qualcomm
list.notes: Qualcomm's US postings give one range for the job code and no zones. It says the range is for the location the job is posted in, but postings open in several offices give one range, and in the postings we read the same range showed in San Diego and Austin.
list.basis_quote: The above pay scale reflects the broad, minimum to maximum, pay scale for this job code for the location for which it has been posted

list.name: Ramp
list.notes: Ramp lists two pay tiers in its job postings. We count SF as the San Francisco-Oakland metro and NY as the New York metro. Its postings say the tier is set by where the candidate is located.
list.basis_quote: For candidates located in NYC or SF

list.name: Rippling
list.notes: Orange County is inside the Los Angeles metro.
list.basis_quote: based on the employee's work location

list.name: Robinhood
list.notes: Robinhood lists its office cities; we matched each to its metro (Menlo Park to San Francisco-Oakland, Bellevue to Seattle, Westlake to Dallas-Fort Worth, Lake Mary to Orlando, Clearwater to Tampa). Its postings say the zone is set by where the work is performed.
list.basis_quote: based on the location where the work will be performed

list.name: Salesforce
list.notes: Salesforce's US postings give a typical range, shown here, and a higher range for some places it doesn't fully name. Two wordings are in use: “select cities within the San Francisco and New York City metropolitan area”, or “California and New York, and select cities in the metropolitan areas of Boston, Chicago, Seattle, and Washington DC”. Slack, Tableau and MuleSoft hire through Salesforce's site.
list.basis_quote: There is a different range applicable to specific work locations

list.name: ServiceTitan
list.notes: ServiceTitan lists two zones by state in its job postings, the same in all 48 US postings that show a range on 24 Nov. A metro that crosses state lines follows the first state in its name, so Philadelphia shows Zone 2 here though its New Jersey side is Zone 1, and Portland shows Zone 2 though Vancouver, WA is Zone 1.
list.basis_quote: For candidates in the United States, the good faith salary ranges estimate for this role is

list.name: Snap
list.notes: Snap puts all of California and Washington in Zone A, but only New York City (not the rest of New York).
list.basis_quote: work locations are assigned a pay zone

list.name: Spotify
list.notes: Spotify's US postings give one “United States base range” and no zones; most US roles are in New York.

list.name: Sprout Social
list.notes: Sprout Social's postings say it has two geographic pay zones in the United States and name the states in each.

list.name: Stripe
list.notes: Stripe's US postings give one annual US range and no zones. For sales roles the range is on-target earnings.
list.basis_quote: will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location

list.name: Temporal
list.notes: Temporal counts a metro as 50 miles from the city centre. The percent is of Tier 1 pay. Sales commission roles (except BDRs) are Tier 1 anywhere. West Palm Beach is in the Miami metro.
list.basis_quote: If your location lies just beyond one of these metro areas

list.name: Toast
list.notes: Toast gives example cities for each zone, not a full list, so only those cities are matched here.
list.basis_quote: determined by office location or, for remote roles, home address (zip code)

list.name: Twilio
list.notes: The tiers appear on a few of Twilio's postings (4 of 114 on 24 Nov), worded the same each time. Tier 2 lists "Maryland" and Tier 3 lists "Maryland (outside of the DC area)"; we read it as the D.C. area in Tier 2 and the rest of Maryland in Tier 3. Areas are matched by metro: the Bay Area as its five metros, the NYC area as the New York metro, the D.C. area as the Washington metro (including its Virginia counties). New Jersey counties in the Philadelphia metro count as Pennsylvania here, which Twilio doesn't list.
list.basis_quote: provided for candidates hired in those locations only

list.name: Twitch
list.notes: Twitch (part of Amazon) posts a range for each city a role is open in, from Seattle, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles and Irvine; which cities appear changes from posting to posting, and it publishes no zone list. We match each city to its metro (Irvine is in the Los Angeles metro).
list.basis_quote: Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location

list.name: UnitedHealth Group
list.notes: UnitedHealth Group's US postings give one salary range and no zones. Its clinical postings give an annual total cash target that includes hourly and incentive pay; those are left out of pay search.
list.basis_quote: Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets

list.name: Veeam
list.notes: Veeam lists four zones in its job postings, the same in all 21 that show them on 24 Nov. Its Zone 1 is the five New York City boroughs only; we match by metro, so Long Island, Westchester and the New Jersey side of the New York metro show Zone 1 here, where Veeam puts the rest of New York in Zone 3 and New Jersey in Zone 4. Veeam also puts sales roles in Georgia, Ohio and Arizona in Zone 3; other roles there are Zone 4, which is what this shows.

list.name: Verily
list.notes: Verily's US postings give one range “across all US locations” and no zones.
list.basis_quote: Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors

list.name: Waymo
list.notes: Waymo's US postings give one range “across US locations” and no zones. Hourly intern rates are left out here.
list.basis_quote: Actual starting pay will be based on job-related factors, including exact work location, experience, relevant training and education, and skill level

list.name: Wing
list.notes: Wing (part of Alphabet) posts one US base range and no zones.
list.basis_quote: Wing’s salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location

list.name: Writer
list.notes: Writer's postings name two tiers; some postings show only one of them. We count SF as the San Francisco-Oakland metro.

list.name: Zillow
list.notes: Zillow's postings give two state groups without naming them; we number them from highest pay. Office roles must live within commuting distance of their office.

list.name: Zoox
list.notes: Zoox (part of Amazon) posts one base range per role and no zones; most roles are in Foster City, CA.
list.basis_quote: Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level
